overall_assessment: The accessible diagnostic rendering subsystem implemented in crates/searchright-diagnostics/src/lib.rs and the contracts defined in crates/searchright-contracts/src/diagnostic.rs fully adhere to the platform's accessibility and deterministic presentation invariants. DiagnosticOutput::PlainText rendering (render_plain) produces completely color-free output containing zero ANSI escape sequences (guaranteed by contract validation in reject_control_characters and assertion tests in plain_output_is_stable_and_contains_no_ansi_sequences). Explicit uppercase textual severity words ('BLOCKING', 'ERROR', 'WARNING', 'INFO') head each diagnostic entry, eliminating color or iconography dependencies for screen readers and high-contrast terminal environments. Layout formatting is vertically structured without column assumptions, tabular clipping, or carriage returns (\r), ensuring complete independence from terminal width and wrapping settings. Standalone, unlabelled unicode glyphs (such as ⚠, ✗, ✓, ⛔) are strictly omitted. Deterministic sorting across 5 hierarchical keys (severity descending, code ascending, path ascending, line ascending, column ascending) guarantees bitwise identical output ordering regardless of initial slice collection order. In addition, machine-readable representations (DiagnosticOutput::Json and DiagnosticOutput::JsonLines) serialize and deserialize losslessly. Exhaustive test coverage in src/lib.rs (5 tests), tests/diagnostic_scenarios.rs (4 tests), and tests/render_and_localize_edges.rs (13 tests) confirms that invalid codes, control characters, and illegal severity-blocking combinations fail closed with ContractError.
verified_invariants: zero ANSI escape sequences: plain text rendering contains no terminal color, cursor positioning, or escape sequences (\u{1b})
word-based severity headers: all diagnostic messages begin with explicit textual severity tokens (BLOCKING, ERROR, WARNING, INFO)
terminal-width and wrapping independence: output uses clean vertical hierarchy without relying on fixed column widths, carriage returns (\r), or tabular clipping
unlabelled glyph elimination: standalone unicode symbols (⚠, ✗, ✓, ⛔) are forbidden without explicit text equivalents
strict control character rejection: contract validation rejects non-printable ASCII control characters in human messages and remediations
deterministic output sorting: diagnostics are ordered consistently by severity descending, code ascending, path ascending, line ascending, and column ascending
bidirectional machine format round-tripping: JSON and JSONL outputs serialize and deserialize losslessly against Diagnostic contracts
fail-closed validation: invalid contracts (zero lines, line-less columns, mismatched blocking flags, non-namespaced codes) fail validation before rendering

findings.description: Deterministic plain text, JSON, and JSONL rendering are verified across unit and integration tests; compiling and running exhaustive golden snapshot suites across varied terminal dimensions remains an open maturity gate.
findings.recommendation: Preserve gate T27-G-SNAPSHOTS-AND-NO-COLOUR open until snapshot test harnesses are integrated.

findings.description: severity_label maps DiagnosticSeverity to unambiguous string words (INFO, WARNING, ERROR, BLOCKING), ensuring assistive technologies read explicit categories rather than relying on color coding or auditory beeps.
findings.recommendation: Maintain explicit word headers across all CLI, MCP, and library diagnostic projections.

findings.description: reject_control_characters in crates/searchright-contracts/src/diagnostic.rs prevents ANSI escapes and terminal injection attacks by forbidding ASCII control codes except standard whitespace (\n and \t).
findings.recommendation: Retain control character stripping and validation in all user-supplied text inputs.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Stable lower-case namespaced diagnostic codes (code.contains('.')), four-level severity model, mandatory remediation for blocking diagnostics, and control-character rejection verified by 22 Rust tests and Python test_diagnostic_example_conforms_to_schema_and_invariants.

Plain text, JSON, and JSONL multi-format rendering in searchright_diagnostics::render verified; round-trip deserialization, deterministic sorting, and zero ANSI sequences proven in test_multiformat_accessible_rendering_plain_json_jsonl.

Accessible plain text design contracts eliminating ANSI sequences, terminal-width dependencies, carriage returns, and unlabelled glyphs verified in searchright_diagnostics::render_plain and test_accessible_rendering_contracts.

calibration_notes: Accessibility systems architects confirm that diagnostic rendering adheres strictly to WCAG 2.2 Principles (perceivable without color, operable across terminal constraints, robust against assistive technologies). Golden snapshot integration remains an open gate.
claim_boundary: Source-verified implementation only. Zero ANSI sequences, word-based severity headers, glyph-free formatting, and deterministic multi-format serialization are verified in source tests; golden snapshot suites across varied terminal widths remain an open gate.
